question: Your team uses Claude Code in a mobile app repository with an ios/ directory and an android/ directory, and each directory has its own CLAUDE.md file. Human-readable standards live in docs/standards/, including swift-style.md and kotlin-style.md. These style guides change every few weeks. The Android maintainer wants Claude Code to follow kotlin-style.md whenever it edits files under android/. What should the Android maintainer do?

options.text: Paste the full text of kotlin-style.md into android/CLAUDE.md, and add a pull request checklist item that reminds engineers to update both copies together.
options.reason: A pasted copy drifts from the source when the guide changes, while @import references the external file and keeps CLAUDE.md modular.

options.text: Write a sentence in android/CLAUDE.md that says a Kotlin style guide exists somewhere in the docs folder and that Claude should look for it when relevant.
options.reason: A vague mention does not include the file's content in the configuration, while an @import reference includes the specific standards file directly.

options.text: Convert kotlin-style.md into a custom slash command in .claude/commands/, and ask Android developers to run that command before each editing session.
options.reason: A slash command runs only when a developer invokes it, so it is not standing configuration; @import is the way to include a standards file in CLAUDE.md.

options.text: Add an @import reference to docs/standards/kotlin-style.md in android/CLAUDE.md so that the guide is included from its single source file.
options.reason: The @import syntax references an external file from CLAUDE.md, which keeps the configuration modular and includes only the standards that are relevant to the package.
